name: Natto gum
lead: Natto gum is a cosmetic ingredient described as a sticky, water-soluble polymer produced by Bacillus bacteria during fermentation of soybeans, as in the Japanese food natto. It is associated with poly-gamma-glutamic acid (gamma-PGA), a water-soluble biodegradable polymer made from glutamic acid.[1][2]
Published sources on natto gum are mostly patents that list it as a moisturising or film-forming ingredient in face packs and creams. No human clinical studies of natto gum were located.

paras: Natto is made by fermenting whole soybeans with Bacillus subtilis var. natto, and its stringy texture is characteristic.[1] Poly-gamma-glutamic acid is a negatively charged, water-soluble polymer produced industrially by Bacillus fermentation; Wikipedia lists it among cosmeceutical uses and describes it as biodegradable and non-immunogenic.[2] The link between natto gum and gamma-PGA is made in ingredient literature rather than in the two Wikipedia pages loaded here, and the exact composition of commercial natto gum was not established from these sources.

Patent documents list natto gum in a Chinese face-pack formulation with nano colloidal silver, aloe and plant extracts,[3] and a Korean patent describes a high-moisturising cosmetic composition combining cellulose gum, natto gum or hyaluronic acid polymer with a phenyl-modified silicone, noting the natto gum is obtained by culturing a Bacillus.[4] These are product descriptions, not efficacy data.

card.summary: A fermented-soybean polymer used as a humectant in face packs; documented in patents, not in trials.

quick.overview:
Natto gum is a sticky polymer from Bacillus fermentation of soybeans, listed in some face packs and moisturisers.

It appears in patents as a moisturising ingredient; no human study was found.
quick.mechanism: It is described as a water-binding, film-forming polymer that holds moisture on the skin, related to poly-gamma-glutamic acid.
quick.risks: No safety data were found in the sources reviewed. Soy-derived ingredients can be an allergen for some people.
